nina: Heads-up: customer reported TS inference loss when importing our SDK from an ESM edge bundle. Generics vanish and `unknown` becomes `any`. Repro attached: https://github.com/redwood/repro-edge-ts-any-unknown-issue omar: ouch. short repro snippet? nina: minimal API:+ ```ts // packages/sdk/src/client.ts export function mutate(input: T): Promise<{ data: T }>; export function mutate(input: unknown) { return Promise.resolve({ data: input as any }); } ``` consumer: ```ts import { mutate } from '@redwood/sdk'; type P = { uid: string }; async function run(){ const got = await mutate

({ uid: 'u' }); // expected: got.data -> P. In ESM edge build it's `any` (no completions). got.data. // no intellisense } ``` nina: The twist: if consumer uses CJS (require) or our cjs entry, types are fine. Only reproducible when the app bundles for Edge (esbuild/rollup) with tsconfig: `module: "esnext"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, and we publish an ESM entry that is a small `export * from './lib'` wrapper. sanjay: Did you diff the generated .d.ts files in the published tarball between cjs and esm entries? nina: Yes. cjs/index.d.ts preserves overloads and generic signatures. esm/index.d.ts in the package tarball shows a single signature with widened parameter types (arg: any) and no generic overload. Seems the bundler or the declaration emitter is collapsing/flattening overloads during the ESM packaging step. omar: Two likely causes: 1) the ESM wrapper is picked up by `tsc --emitDeclarationOnly` and it doesn't see the original overload declarations, so it emits a merged/widened declaration; 2) our publish pipeline uses esbuild to produce an ESM bundle and then runs a dts bundler that loses overloads. Also check `types`/`typesVersions` in package.json. sanjay: Also check TS flags that affect emit: `preserveValueImports`, `declarationMap`, `composite`, and `skipLibCheck` (less likely). `preserveValueImports` changes how imports are represented and can influence whether TS resolves individual declaration nodes for overload resolution. nina: quick repro for maintainers: untar the published package and compare d.ts ```sh npm pack . # produce sdk-1.2.3.tgz tar -xzf sdk-1.2.3.tgz package/dist/esm/index.d.ts package/dist/cjs/index.d.ts git diff --no-index package/dist/cjs/index.d.ts package/dist/esm/index.d.ts ``` om ar: (lol) small typo in your snippet but clear. build-bot: Created issue RW-DX-7021: "ESM packaging + bundler collapses SDK overloads and widens generics/unknown to any for Edge consumers" (priority: P2). Repro attached. sanjay: short-term mitigation for users: recommend importing the cjs entry until fix: `import { mutate } from '@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs'` or add an explicit types-only import that points to the preserved d.ts. Also add a troubleshooting blurb in the SDK README. omar: Plan for fix: 1) add CI step that emits declarations for both cjs & esm artifacts (fail if public API differs), 2) change ESM packaging to avoid producing a thin re-export wrapper (point `exports.import` at the compiled esm file that already has correct d.ts), 3) if bundler must be used, run `api-extractor` or `dts-bundle-generator` to produce a curated index.d.ts that preserves overloads. If needed, hand-author a stable index.d.ts for the public surface. sanjay: Also add a tiny consumer test that installs the tarball in a fixture app (esbuild/vercel edge) and runs `npx tsc --noEmit` to ensure intellisense/generic inference works. That will prevent regressions in future packaging changes. docs: I'll add the README note + a short troubleshooting snippet plus the deep-import workaround. Also link the issue. nina: one extra gotcha we discovered: when `types` in package.json points to a top-level types file but `exports` maps the import entry to a different file, TypeScript sometimes prefers the d.ts closest to the resolved JS entry. So we need to ensure `types`/`exports` align or provide `typesVersions` to guide resolution. om ar: Great point. Types resolution matrix: exports.import -> the resolved path's .d.ts wins. If our bundler overwrote that file with a flattened d.ts, TS will pick the flattened one. sanjay: I'll pick up the CI + packaging changes. kevin/nina can pair if needed on api-extractor config. build-bot: Linked PR #489 in issue RW-DX-7021 (WIP): add declaration-emit check + consumer fixture. nina: thanks all. I'll attach customer repro and add a tiny vercel edge sample to our mono repo so we can catch this in presubmit. :sparkles:
